title: The star cluster NGC 3572 and its dramatic surroundings
caption: The star cluster NGC 3572 and its surroundings, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Clouds of gas and dust around the young star cluster NGC 3572 have been carved into playful bubbles and arcs, along with curious shapes called elephant trunks, in this image from ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile. The shaping is done by stellar winds flowing from the cluster's bright stars.

NGC 3572 is a gathering of young stars, and ESO describes this as the best image of it so far, made with the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope's Wide Field Imager. Elephant trunks are dense columns of gas and dust that resist erosion by the winds and radiation of nearby stars, leaving pillar-like shapes behind.

The cluster's brightest members outweigh the Sun, and their brief lives will finish in supernova explosions. Massive stars burn through their fuel much faster than lower-mass ones, which is why the most luminous members of a young cluster are also the shortest-lived.

understand.summary: This image from the Wide Field Imager combines B and V filters with a hydrogen-alpha filter. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Long camera exposures and a hydrogen-alpha filter reveal faint glowing gas that the eye could not see.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture combines two visible-light filters, B and V, with a hydrogen-alpha filter that isolates the glow of hydrogen gas in the surrounding clouds. NGC 3572 lies in the direction of the constellation Carina.
alt: A young star cluster surrounded by clouds of gas and dust shaped into bubbles, arcs and elephant trunks.
